sources.title: Taming Throughput-Latency Tradeoff in LLM Inference with Sarathi-Serve
sources.authors: Amey Agrawal, Nitin Kedia, Ashish Panwar, Jayashree Mohan, Nipun Kwatra, Bhargav S. Gulavani, Alexey Tumanov, Ramachandran Ramjee
sources.readset: Full paper, references and artifact appendix read; case claims checked against sections 4.1-4.3, section 5 setup, Figure 9, Figure 14, Table 4 and section 6. Key physical PDF pages 8, 9, 10, 11, 13 and 14 visually inspected during grounding; curves were not digitized.
sources.rights_note: Publisher open access establishes readability, not a blanket redistribution or adaptation license. Only an original attributed explanation is packaged; raw PDF, extracted text, images, figures and supplier synthesis are excluded.

applicability: Source-supported hypothesis selection when observed long prefills interfere with ongoing decodes
Chunked-prefill token-budget tradeoffs under specified latency, workload, hardware and parallelism conditions
limitations: Paper-author observations and proposed adaptation checks are not local measurements or current-engine support.
The combined design does not beat hybrid-only P50 TTFT in either Table 4 trace.
No universal budget, fairness guarantee, quantitative disaggregation comparison or empirical skill efficacy is established.
Raw source redistribution and adaptation permission remain UNKNOWN.

The same case identity and central mechanism appeared in closed-unmerged PR 156; this independently written fixed-edition contribution does not recover the missing historical archive or establish novelty over its unavailable synthesis.
attribution: Original attributed explanation of Agrawal et al., OSDI 2024. The paper's reported results remain distinct from InferRSI's proposed checks; no raw source asset or prior proposal prose is reproduced.

findings.direction: Subtract active decode tokens before filling a mixed batch with prefill
findings.reason: Sarathi-Serve budgets one token per ongoing decode first, then accounts for partial prefills and admits new prompt chunks with the remaining budget and allocation capacity. The extra work can still extend a decode iteration.
findings.revisit_when: Confirm trace evidence of prefill interference and verify that the target engine’s mixed batch implements the same ordering before adapting the policy.

findings.direction: Compare the token-gap gain from smaller chunks with repeated launch and KV costs
findings.reason: Smaller chunks bound prefill work per iteration but can reduce utilization and repeat fixed overhead. Later chunks attend back over earlier prompt chunks, causing extra KV-cache reads even though total attention computation is unchanged.
findings.revisit_when: Profile candidate sizes on the actual device and report prefill time, sustained throughput and token gaps together.

findings.direction: Sample tile boundaries and stage imbalance when tuning chunk length
findings.reason: The paper identifies tile boundaries and uneven pipeline batch runtimes as sources of nonlinear cost. Larger chunks can leave stages idle, while very small chunks also lose efficiency.
findings.revisit_when: Under the intended model and parallelism, profile nearby lengths on both sides of tile boundaries and include pipeline idle time when applicable.

findings.direction: Read the reported TTFT and TBT comparison as a workload-conditioned trade
findings.reason: For both Table 4 traces, the combined design lowered P99 TBT versus either component alone. Median TTFT was below chunked-only and above hybrid-only in that setup.
findings.revisit_when: Preserve separate percentile and load definitions before borrowing this comparison for a new service configuration.
findings.bounds: 128 requests, Yi-34B on two A100s, 1024-token budget, separately for OpenChat and arXiv summarization.

findings.direction: Freeze matched arrival, queueing and latency objectives before changing a serving budget
findings.reason: The reported capacity work combined a model-specific token-gap objective with a scheduling-delay limit and defined request length filters. An improvement to one latency number alone does not settle the deployment tradeoff.
findings.revisit_when: Hold workload, model, hardware, runtime and parallelism constant. Measure TTFT, TBT, scheduling delay and sustainable throughput and keep the incumbent when the required evidence is missing.
